title: Testing and safely rolling out OTA updates

questions.prompt: Which option states the main idea of “Testing and safely rolling out OTA updates” correctly?
options: For safer ESP32 updates, flash can hold the running application and another app slot.
OTA (Over-The-Air) updates a device over a network instead of plugging in a USB cable.
This example uploads from Arduino IDE to a supported ESP32 on the same Wi-Fi network.

questions.prompt: Which additional fact about “Testing and safely rolling out OTA updates” is accurate?
options: The first setup still needs USB: install a sketch with Wi-Fi and OTA support over the cable, then later uploads can use the network.
The new image is written to the inactive slot
For example, new firmware can be sent over Wi-Fi to a greenhouse sensor.
updating hundreds at once is risky.
questions.answer: updating hundreds at once is risky.
questions.explanation: updating hundreds at once is risky.

questions.prompt: Which practical detail should be considered when using “Testing and safely rolling out OTA updates”?
options: OTA makes remote maintenance easier, but the device needs a safe recovery path if power or connectivity fails.
after reboot, the device performs basic health checks.
A staged rollout updates a test device first, then a small group, and expands only after success.
questions.answer: A staged rollout updates a test device first, then a small group, and expands only after success.
questions.explanation: A staged rollout updates a test device first, then a small group, and expands only after success.

questions.prompt: Which statement from the “Testing and safely rolling out OTA updates” lesson is correct?
options: Before updating, verify the board model, firmware version, file size, and cryptographic signature.
If they pass, the new image is confirmed.
The key difference is how firmware reaches the board: USB/serial needs a computer and cable nearby
questions.answer: Before updating, verify the board model, firmware version, file size, and cryptographic signature.
